chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the urine of a young child. He said: “You pour water over it; but if he has already eaten, then wash it with water thoroughly. And the boy and the girl are equal in this ruling.”

key_terms.الصَّبِيِّ: young child; the subject whose urine is being asked about
key_terms.الْجَارِيَةُ: girl; the other child category, stated to have the same ruling
key_terms.الْغُلَامُ: boy; one of the two child categories mentioned
key_terms.الْمَاءَ: water; the means of purification mentioned in the hadith
key_terms.بَوْلِ: urine; the impurity being discussed in the legal ruling
key_terms.تَصُبُّ: you pour; indicating pouring water over the affected area
key_terms.غَسْلًا: a washing; an emphatic expression for proper washing
key_terms.فَاغْسِلْهُ: then wash it; indicating a fuller washing after the child has eaten

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on purifying clothing or other things from the urine of an infant in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on purifying urine from a young child. It distinguishes between the child who has not yet eaten and the one who has begun eating, and it states that the ruling applies equally to both boys and girls.
